chapter: Black and Tan and Kansas City nightlife
title: After-hours, breakfast shows and jamming around Kansas City
summary: After closing at four or five, musicians went to after-hours joints and breakfast shows, and jammed in daytime bars.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah. I had a...once in awhile, we go and a play after we got off early in the mornin'. Nobody went home. We go to the after-hours joints...house rent parties.
After-hours was after five? You mean the club was open till five, and...

We close...we close about four o'clock...about four or five o'clock. After that, we go...all the clubs done close... we talk about have a breakfast show at different clubs. They start at five o'clock in the morning...nightclubs' business was boomin'. And we go. We get off from work, close up. Other joints'd be opening up, have a floorshow an' everything. We get outta these joints at ten and twelve o'clock in the daytime...when the show would be over. So we be up probably all night and half o' the day. Didn't have nothin' else to do. Then the people tell you the cats'd go to different bars in the daytime, sit around and jam.
Who all was playing in Kansas City then?
Well, I don't remember all them people. Fact is, I don't remember all them people's names. Lemme see. Let me see. I just saw some of them people about five years ago.
When you made that film? ["Last of the Blue Devils"]
Yeah. I really don't remember. Close it [the tape recorder] off a minute.

Yeah, we stay out till five o'clock in the mornin'. When we got off, we go stay all...half o' the day in another nightclub. Had a lot of entertainers. I had never been off of Independence Avenue. Finally,
